criteria.text: The response concludes that the SOW's choice of California law and exclusive San Francisco County forum overrides the License Agreement's Delaware law and Wilmington, Delaware forum for implementation disputes, so related claims would be split between two laws and two forums. It identifies the location as the SOW's governing law and venue section (Section 9), explains why this matters to Fatesk, and recommends a fix.
hints: laws of the State of California

criteria.text: The response concludes that the SLA Schedule's narrow 'Severity 1 Incident' definition (complete unavailability to all End Users in all regions) controls over the License Agreement's definition (unavailability to 10% or more of End Users), undermining the License Agreement's Severity 1 protections. It identifies the location as the Service Level Schedule Section 2.1, explains why this matters to Fatesk, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Drupuv can assign the License Agreement without Fatesk's consent to any person, including a Fatesk competitor, contrary to the term sheet. It identifies the location as License Agreement Section 15.2 and/or the 'Permitted Transfer' definition in Section 1, explains why this matters to Fatesk, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the License Agreement automatically renews for successive three-year terms unless notice of non-renewal is given within a 30-day window between 150 and 120 days before term end, departing from the term sheet's one-year renewals with 90 days' notice. It identifies the location as License Agreement Section 12.2, explains why this matters to Fatesk, and recommends a fix.

The response states that the License Agreement's order-of-precedence clause (Section 17.4) gives the SOW and/or the SLA Schedule priority over the License Agreement within their respective subject areas.
The response states that the annual license fee is $1,840,000 per contract year.
The response is a memo addressed to the supervising partner that, for each issue, gives the document and section where it appears, why it matters for Fatesk, and a recommended fix.
The response claims that the License Agreement's Delaware governing law and Wilmington forum govern disputes over Implementation Services under the SOW.
The response claims that the License Agreement renews for one-year renewal terms.
